object.proposition: The December 2023 settlement of Synergy CHC Corp. v. HVL, LLC d/b/a Atrium Innovations created a loan payable of $5,450,000. At June 30, 2024 the outstanding balance was $4,802,445, and the schedule requires $2,000,000 in 2024, $2,000,000 in 2025 and $802,445 in 2026. Linking the Note 11 '$5,450,000 December 28, 2023 Loan' (described as a settlement with a 'former supplier') to Atrium, and to the 'Atrium' row in the notes-payable table, is an inference based on Note 13's cross-reference and the matching $5,450,000 and $4,802,445 amounts. The unchanged balance between Dec 31, 2023 and June 30, 2024 suggests that none of the 2024 installment was paid by June 30 (also an inference).

payload.fact: How much of the $2,000,000 2024 installment on the Atrium settlement loan, and of the $600,000 2024 installment on the March 27, 2024 supplier settlement loan, did Synergy CHC Corp. pay between June 30 and August 13, 2024? What are the exact due dates of the unpaid remainder through December 31, 2024?
payload.why_pivotal: Neither loan's balance changed between Dec 31, 2023 and Jun 30, 2024 for Atrium, and only $100,000 was paid on the supplier loan in 2024 through June 30. With ~$2.0M of reported cash and a $200K reserve, the cumulative condition requires $800K–$900K of net operating cash by year-end if 0% was paid, $150K–$250K if 25% was paid, and nothing if at least 50% was paid. The 6-month advance's ~$44K monthly payments would be added on top.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Settlement agreement payment schedules (Atrium; supplier), bank statements or payment confirmations after June 30, 2024, or a borrower-certified debt schedule as of the decision date
payload.if_resolved: If at least half was paid, or the remainder is due late in December, reported cash covers the settlements and reserve, and the $100K or $250K 6-month offers could be assessed on operating receipts. If mostly unpaid with near-term due dates, the settlements alone use up all cash. That would favor the smallest offer or deferral, and the 3-month $250K offer (about $86K per month) would be least feasible.

payload.fact: Has Knight Therapeutics consented to, or waived its covenant for, a new $100,000–$250,000 unsecured or subordinated working-capital advance to Synergy CHC Corp.? The covenant says 'Synergy shall not add any other debt without paying out KTI first'.
payload.why_pivotal: Without consent, any permitted offer could breach the senior-secured Knight loan ($12.3M), with default provisions and cross-default into the Sanders loan ($9.8M). Knight holds a senior lien on all current and future assets, so the advance would rank behind Knight.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Written consent or waiver from Knight Therapeutics, an amended loan agreement, or a permitted-debt carve-out clause in the Knight Sixth Amendment
payload.if_resolved: If Knight consents or a carve-out exists, the choice depends on cash timing (settlement installments and operating receipts). If not, no offer can be treated as permissible regardless of cash sufficiency.

payload.summary: Synergy CHC Corp.'s litigation with its former contract manufacturer (HVL, LLC d/b/a Atrium Innovations) was settled in December 2023. The settlement created a $5,450,000 loan payable at 5% interest. The balance at June 30, 2024 was $4,802,445 (unchanged from Dec 31, 2023), and the schedule requires $2,000,000 in 2024 (fnd_002). Linking this loan to Atrium relies on Note 13's cross-reference plus matching amounts and the 'Atrium' row, so it is an inference (fnd_003). A second confidential supplier settlement (March 27, 2024; $2,920,824 outstanding) requires $600,000 in 2024 (fnd_005); linking it to the 'VitBest' row is also an amount-match inference. The $2,235,986 Atrium gain was booked as a reduction of FY2023 cost of sales. It is noncash and nonrecurring (fnd_006, eff_003). The Valenti settlement ($340K, paid 2023) and the L.O.D.C. settlement (paid May 2024) are resolved and have no cash effect (fnd_008, fnd_009, eff_004). Separately, the senior-secured Knight loan says 'Synergy shall not add any other debt without paying out KTI first' (fnd_007, eff_005). Sensitivity uses ~$2.0M reported cash at Aug 12, 2024 and a $200K illustrative reserve, and counts only the two settlement installments. If nothing was paid after June 30, $800K of net operating cash is needed by year-end ($900K if the $100K restricted cash is unavailable). At 25% paid, $150K–$250K is needed. At 50% or more paid, nothing is needed. This excludes the advance's own payments ($44,167/month for $250K over 6 months; $17,667 for $100K; $85,833 for $250K over 3 months), the Kenek related-party short-term loan, the WebBank/Shopify merchant loans (sales-linked, which the Knight covenant requires to be repaid by Dec 31, 2024), and Knight monthly interest. All of these are already within the ~$4.1M of indebtedness due in 2024 and must not be added twice.
pivotal_unknowns: Amount of the $2,000,000 Atrium and $600,000 supplier 2024 settlement installments paid between 2024-06-30 and 2024-08-13, and due dates of the remainder
Whether Knight Therapeutics consents to or carves out new debt despite 'Synergy shall not add any other debt without paying out KTI first'
Whether the ~$2.0M cash figure at 2024-08-12 includes the $100,000 restricted cash
payload.conclusion: No conclusion yet on whether to fund. Two pivotal facts are missing. (1) Knight Therapeutics' consent: the senior-secured Knight loan bars any other debt without first paying out Knight, so no offer can be treated as permissible without a consent, waiver or carve-out. (2) How much of the 2024 settlement installments (Atrium $2.0M; supplier $600K) was paid between June 30 and Aug 13, 2024, and when the rest is due. Unpaid, they alone use up the ~$2.0M reported cash and the reserve. If Knight consents and at least half the installments were paid, the smaller 6-month offer ($100K) and then the $250K 6-month request can be assessed on operating receipts. The 3-month $250K offer has the largest monthly payments and is least compatible with the year-end settlement cash demand. The identifications of the Atrium and VitBest rows are inferences from matching amounts. The lawsuits' severity is not turned into any default probability or dollar adjustment.
